title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Labor Element Behind a Response Credit
content:
Where a demand service charge line of the labor kind stands on the rate program for the call the credit
arises from, the labor element is that line.

Where no such line stands and the tier sells no prepaid hours at all, the labor element is nil.

Where a line of that kind stands, the first term governs; where none stands and the tier does sell
prepaid hours, neither term takes the labor element from the ticket's own valuation.

**Which programs sell no prepaid hours at all** is read from the hours a block carries under each
program of the Demand Service Rate Programs; where that figure stands at 0 the program sells none:

| Program | Hours credited by a block |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 0 |
| Priority Response Program | 0 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 40 |
| Emergency Response Program | 80 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 120 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 200 |

| A labor-kind charge line on the rate program for that call | The program's block hours | The labor element |
|---|---|---|
| stands | any | that line |
| does not stand | 0, the program selling no prepaid hours | nil |
| does not stand | above 0 | neither term above takes it from the ticket's own valuation |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On the Time & Material Account, which carries 0 block hours, a credit
worked out where no labor-kind charge line stands on the program for the call has a labor element of
nil. On the Emergency Response Program, whose blocks carry 80 hours, the same absence of a line does not
make the labor element nil.
